Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG LEGAL OPINION NO.JJ7 S. 2010 VICE MAYOR EFREN R. ARATEA San Antonio, Zambales Dear Vice Mayor Aratea: This has reference to your letter dated 05 July 2010 requesting the Department's legal opinion on whether or not you, as Vice Mayor of San Antonio, Zambales, are legally required to assume the Office of the Municipal Mayor in view of the disqualification to hold office of Mayor- elect Romeo D. Lonzanida (hereinafter referred to as "Lonzanida") by reason of the latter's conviction by final judgment of the crime of falsification of public documents which is punishable by imprisonment of four (4) years and one (I) day of prision correctional as minimum penalty to eight (8) years and one (I) day of prision mayor as maximum penalty. On the other hand, on 08 July 2010, this Department also received a letter from Dra. Estela D. Antipolo, a candidate for the mayoralty race in San Antonio, Zambales, who received the second highest number of votes, second to disqualified Lonzanida. In said letter, Dra. Antipolo advised us that prior to the May 2010 elections, a Petition to Disqualify and/or Cancel Certificate of Candidacy was filed by Dra. Sigrid S. Rodolfo against Lonzanida before the COMELEC, docketed as SPA 09-158 on the ground of Lonzanida's violation of the three (3) consecutive term rule provided in the 1987 Constitution and the Local Government Code of 1991. As a result thereof, the COMELEC 2nd Division issued a Resolution on 18 February 2010 ordering the cancellation and striking off Lonzanida's name in the list of official candidates for the position of Mayor of San Antonio, Zambales. Thereafter, Lonzanida filed a Motion for Reconsideration from said Resolution which, to date, is pending Resolution before the COMELEC En Banc. In the light of the pendency of the resolution of Lonzanida's Motion for Reconsideration, this Department deemed it wise to refer the said letter of Dra. Estela D. Antipolo to the COMELEC for appropriate action. In reply to your request for opinion, we would like to stress that at the outset, regardless of whether or not Lonzanida took an oath of office prior to his assumption of duties as mayor, i.e., as the issuance of the questioned Memoranda, he is disqualified to be a candidate, let alone hold said office based on paragraph I, Sec. 12 of the Omnibus Election Code (BP Big. 881), to wit: "SEC. 12. Disqualifications.- Any person who has been declared by competent authority insane or incompetent, or has

-2- been sentenced by final jndgnwnt for subversion, insurrection, rebellion, or for any offense for which he has been sentenced to a penalty of more than eighteen months or for a crime involving moral turpitude, shall be disqualified to be a candidate and to hold any office, unless he has been given plenary pardon or granted antnesty. " It may be recalled that on 26 February 2010, this Department had answered a similar query from then San Antonio, Zambales Vice Mayor Ragadio under identical circumstances in DILG Opinion No. 15, s. 2010. In said legal opinion, we opined that Mayor Romeo D. Lonzanida is disqualified to hold the Office of the Mayor by reason of his criminal conviction. As a consequence thereof, the Office of the Mayor is deemed permanently vacant. The Vice Mayor is then mandated under Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1 991 (RA 7160) to assume said office. In view of the foregoing, you, as Vice Mayor of said municipality, shall assume the Office of the Mayor in an acting capacity without prejudice to the COMELEC's resolution of the Motion for Reconsideration filed by Lonzanida. Hereto attached is a photocopy of the aforesaid DILG Opinion for your ready perusal. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUS RE A. Accused Mayor Lonzanida elevated the case to the Supreme Court where : Fhe Highest Court promulgated on 20 July 2009 a Decision affirming the Decision ated 25 July 2003 and Resolution dated 24 September 2003 of the ndiganbayan (Fourth Division). On 23 October 2009, the aforesaid Decision of i!he Supreme Court became final and executory and was, accordingly, recorded in he Book of Entries of Judgments. ' For such finality of judgment, a Bench Warrant of Arrest dated 08 $ebruary 2010 was issued by the Sandiganbayan (Fourth Division) against -accused Mayor Lonzanida. Said Warrant of Arrest was received by the San ; I iöntonio Police Station on 15 February 2010 but they could not serve the same to accused Mayor Lonzanida since the latter could not be located. According to you, accused Mayor Lonzanida has not been reporting to his ffice since 15 February 2010 so that on 22 February 2010, you assumed as cting Municipal Mayor thereat. Hence, you are now asking this Department's legal opinion regarding the egality of your assumption as Acting Mayor and the legal consequence of ccused Mayor Lonzanida's continued hiding. You also would like to inquire on he legality of accused Mayor Lonzanida's signing of official documents despite I this criminal conviction, standing warrant of arrest and non-appearance in his fficé. i We shall answer your queries in one (1) discussion considering that they r&all interrelated. In reply thereto, allow us first to restate the peltinent provision of the Ilocal Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160). Section 44 provides and we quote: "SECTION 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offi ces of the Governor , Vice-Governor, Mayor ; ! Nayor If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the governor or mayor, the vice-governor or vice-mayor concerned shali become the governor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs in the offices of the governor, vice-governor, mayor, or Vice-mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian ernber, shan become the governor, vice-governor, mayor or vice-mayor, as the case may be. Subsequent vacancies in the said office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined therein. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or permanently to discharge the functions of his office. (Emphasis Supplied) ii: It may be observed that the last paragraph of the aforequoted provision numerated the specific causes of permanent vacancies. Such enumeration was Ilowed by a general statement, to wit: "xxxis otherwise permanently

Inca citated , to discharge the functions of his office". This general ütement may refer to permanent vacancies brought about by application of 'laws, such as civil interdiction or disqualification to hold office as an accessory énal to criminal conviction, such as in the case of Mayor Lonzanida. i; Aon ce i Lon It bears to note that a criminal conviction carries with it certain inherent ry penalties which operate as a disqualification from holding public office. ted in the narration of facts above, the decision convicting Mayor nida of the abovestated offense has already become final and executory. Inality therefore of said Decision would warrant the application of the ry penalties. The penalty of prision mayor, the most severe penalty meted upon Mayor nida, carries with it the inherent accessory penalties of temporary absolute (9squ lification and that of perpetual special disqualification from the right of ge (Article 42, Revised Penal Code). In this regard, may we invite you to e f ilowing provisions of the Revised Penal Code: "ART. 30. Effect of the penalties of perpetual or temporary absolute disqua i fication.—The penalties of I l' perpetual or temporary absolute disqualification for public office shall produce the following effects: I. The deprivation of the public offices and employments which the offender may have held, even if conferred by popular election. The deprivation of the right to vote in any elect!on for any popular elective office or to be elected to such office. The disqualification for the offices or public employments and for the exercise of any of the rights mentioned. In cases of temporary disqualification, such disqualification as is comprised in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this article shall last during the term of the sentence." "ART, 32. Effects of t: he penalties of perpetual or temporary special disqualification for the exercise of the ; right of suffrage.—The perpetual or temporary special disqualification for the exercise of the right of suffrage shall deprive the offender perpetually or daring the term of the sentence, according to the nature of said penalty, of the right to vote in any popular election for any public office or to be elected to such office. Moreover, the offender shan not be permitted to hold any public office during the period of his disq ualification." Based on the foregoing, the accessory penalties of temporary absolute 'squ lification and that of perpetual special disqualification from the right of s' ff ge operate to deprive the offender of the public office, which he may have héld. Otherwise stated, these accessory penalties that are inherent to the penalty impo d upon Mayor Lonzanida, would permanently incapacitate him from furth r discharging the functions of his office, including that of signing official : docu ents appurtenant to the Office of the Mayor. Such permanent incapacity

C)? th Bart: of Mayor Lonzanida will thus give rise to the existence of a rmanent vacancy in the office of the mayor. There being a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor, you, as the , • Oice-Mayor thereat shall become the mayor applying the aforequoted provision c)' Ction 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991. 'On a final note, if Mayor Lonzanida shall insists on signing official documents appurtenant to the Office of the Mayor despite his criminal conviction ang its corresponding accessory penalties, he may again be opening himself to a possible criminat charge of usurpation of authority.
